text:
elaine: quick heads-up — acme wants to run a private-deploy POC next week. they need: a PrivateLink path from their VPC to our connector, a static egress IP (their security team requires allowlist), and clarity on firewall rules when TLS inspection is in the path. also asking how PrivateLink vs NAT egress impacts pricing for the POC. @mike can you confirm technical blockers?

mike (solutions): basic flow looks fine. PrivateLink (interface endpoint) in their account -> our connector in their private subnets. that keeps traffic on AWS backbone (no public internet hop). for a static outbound IP from their side they can provision a NAT gateway with EIP in their account, or they can route through their existing egress proxy. if they want us to terminate egress on our side (we proxy outbound calls) that introduces compliance questions (data egress control + cost).

elaine: they specifically said they run TLS inspection on their perimeter and will re-sign TLS. will that break anything?

mike (solutions): TLS inspect that re-terminates TLS will remove original SNI and cert chain — if they do intercept, host-based allowlisting (FQDN) becomes harder. two pragmatic options:
- recommend PrivateLink + interface endpoint: traffic never leaves AWS and SNI survives between client and our service if inspection is not in-line on the path.
- if inspection must happen, ask them to allow our endpoint IPs and/or hostnames on their inspection device. we can provide a short IP/FQDN list for the POC.

mike (solutions): sample minimal firewall / allowlist snippet they can drop into their NGFW:
```
# outbound allowlist from customer firewall -> our connector
Allow TCP 443 to: connect.redwood-inference.us-east-1.internal (or customer-specific endpoint IPs)
Allow UDP 123 to NTP pool (if they restrict time sync)
Allow UDP/TCP 53 to their DNS resolver (or allow DNS over TLS to their resolver)
```

sam (security): for the security questionnaire bits: we encrypt all control-plane and data-plane traffic in transit with TLS 1.2+/ECDHE; for Private Deploy customers we support customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption (ask for key ARN during onboarding). we do not persist customer prompt payloads in logs beyond short ephemeral traces for debugging unless the customer opts in. i'll draft precise questionnaire answers if you send the doc.

tyler (pricing): quick pricing note: PrivateLink has both endpoint-hour charges and per-GB data processing charges (varies by region). NAT-egress incurs data transfer out costs + NAT gateway hourly/EIP. for short POCs we usually model both and show delta. rough ballpark: PrivateLink can be cheaper if traffic stays within AZ and avoids inter-AZ data transfer and long-distance transfer, but NAT + BYOIP/EIP might be simpler for customers who already have egress infra. i can run a 30-day estimate for the expected GB/day — send me volumes.

elaine: customer asked whether we can provide a single static IP they can allow on a firewall (they don't want to manage DNS FQDNs).

mike (solutions): two ways:
1) customer NAT + single EIP in their account -> simplest from their ops side.
2) we can front them with a proxy that uses our EIP, but that means customer traffic exits their environment to our managed egress and triggers security review. we can do it for POC with a written exception, but it's not default for enterprise due to data residency controls.

elaine: they also asked about SNI preservation when using an SNI-stripping TLS inspect device + PrivateLink — will our service break?

mike (solutions): if TLS is intercepted and re-signed by their device, the client-side SNI will be whatever the inspector presents. as long as their inspector preserves SNI extension when re-establishing TLS (many enterprise appliances do) we’re fine. otherwise, allowlisting by IP for the POC is the safe path.

sam (security): for the questionnaire, also remind them that Private Deploy can run with a private control plane (no public control plane endpoints exposed) and we support VPC endpoints for our management plane. we can include that in the answers.

tyler (pricing): i can model both. elaine — estimated dataset: how many GB/day for generation/embeddings? and required concurrent qps for the POC? i'll pre-fill costs for: PrivateLink (endpoint + data), NAT with EIP, and proxy option.

elaine: told them 20GB/day and ~5 qps peak. i'll send the contact info and security questionnaire doc to sam. also they want a short one-pager with the exact ports/hosts to hand to their netsec.

mike (solutions): i'll author a 1-pager with exact IP ranges/FQDN patterns and a small diagram. tagging @deploy-bot to attach the latest connector config sample.

deploy-bot: connector-config-v3.yaml uploaded to Acme POC folder: /onboarding/acme/poc/connector-config-v3.yaml :thumbsup:

elaine: perfect — i'll loop in acme and get their approval on the proxy vs NAT approach. if we need to escalate to enterprise compliance for proxy exceptions i'll raise with legal. thanks all.

sam (security): i'll start drafting questionnaire answers and call out the KMS key ARNs we'll need.

tyler (pricing): i'll post a cost snapshot by EOD after i run the calcs.

elaine: closing summary: next actions — mike provide 1-pager + IP/FQDN list, sam drafts questionnaire answers, tyler runs POC cost model, elaine to schedule kickoff with customer.
